evidence: `src/workflows/work-on.ts` has two merge paths: dispatcher parent-node merge and direct finalization merge.

Both paths currently perform merge bookkeeping before their first merged-label projection; the direct path completes the merge phase before calling `#projectWorkflowStage`, while the dispatcher path records the merge effect first.

Post-merge artifact, close, cleanup, terminal projection, and completion operations can throw after the merge API succeeds; the completion handlers persist failure without guaranteeing a new projection attempt.
`#reconcileWorkflowProjection` can recover a merged label from durable terminal/merge state, but that is restart/reconciliation dependent and does not protect the in-process failure window.
`test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` currently covers label mapping but not ordering across a successful merge and failing follow-up work.

## Investigation Report

### What Was Claimed

A successful durable merge can remain projected with `workflow:awaiting-merge` because the `workflow:merged` label is attempted only after post-merge work. If that work fails, the completion path records failure without retrying the label projection.

### What We Found

The finding is valid in the current integration branch. The dispatcher parent-node merge and direct finalization merge each duplicate the merge sequence. Their first merged-label projection occurs only after merge bookkeeping (`effect.recorded` and, in direct finalization, `phase.completed`). Later review-completion artifacts, issue closure, cleanup, terminal artifacts, and run completion remain throwable. A final projection during terminal rendering or restart reconciliation is not an in-process guarantee.

### Root Cause

Merged workflow projection is not centralized at the merge API success boundary. The implementation allows durable bookkeeping and subsequent post-merge operations to run before the earliest guaranteed projection attempt, leaving an avoidable window in which an actually merged pull request still carries `workflow:awaiting-merge`.

### Affected Files

| Path | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Centralize and invoke merged-label projection immediately after either merge path receives a successful merge result. |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Add focused ordering regression coverage for projection before follow-up work. |

### Evidence

- `#runParentNode` calls `github.mergePullRequest`, then records the merge effect, and only then calls `#projectWorkflowStage(link, "merged", ...)`.
- `#finalize` calls `github.mergePullRequest`, then records the merge effect and completes the merge phase, and only then calls `#projectWorkflowStage(link, "merged", ...)`.
- `postReviewCompletionArtifacts`, issue close, cleanup, terminal artifacts, and `run.completed` follow the merge operation and can reject independently.
- `#projectWorkflowStage` already performs bounded idempotent retries and warns instead of converting durable progress into a false failure; the fix should preserve that behavior and retain later reconciliation calls.

### History Findings

The issue carries the source review fingerprint from PR #117 (`workflow-correctness-001`). No unrelated history or scope expansion is required; repository guidance requires a focused regression test for recovery/safety fixes.

### Recommendation

Introduce one small merge-result sequencing helper in `src/workflows/work-on.ts`. It should await the merge operation, invoke the existing merged workflow projection immediately on success, and return the merge result. Use it in both merge paths before effect/phase bookkeeping and post-merge artifacts. Keep terminal/reconciliation projections as idempotent fallbacks. Verify with a callback-order test that the merged projection happens before follow-up work even when that work fails.

### Related Issues

- #119 (current remediation)
- #117 (source pull request carrying the finding)

### Decomposition Assessment

Single bounded workflow correction; decomposition is not required.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Reproduce/validate the merge-to-projection failure window on the current integration branch.
- [ ] Project `workflow:merged` immediately after successful merge in both supported merge paths.
- [ ] Preserve idempotent retry and restart reconciliation behavior.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage for projection-before-follow-up ordering.
- [ ] Run the required `check` verification and obtain a fresh full review of the exact remediation head.
